modules.name: docs-puller
modules.purpose: Local-first documentation retrieval for engineers and AI agents. Mirror vendor and project docs to Markdown, index them with SQLite FTS5, search on the machine, and prove quality with a rerunnable public BM25 sample eval.
architecture: Docs sources crawl or mirror into a Markdown corpus.
A SQLite FTS5 index is built with a pure Go driver.
Search uses BM25. Optional embeddings and LLM rerank are additive upgrades, not the honest public floor.
An eval harness publishes Hit@1 and Hit@5 on a pinned public sample.
The Apache-2.0 local CLI is the pin. A hosted Team control plane is not this public tree.
decisions: Local-first privacy by default: no cloud account is required to search.
Eval is a product feature. Public sample BM25 is published and rerunnable.
The flattering maintainer private-corpus suite is not the number a hiring manager can replay.
Open-core boundary: free local CLI versus hosted control plane.
talking_points: Lead AI-infrastructure pin: retrieval plus release discipline.
Public BM25 sample reached 95.8% Hit@1 and 100% Hit@5 on pinned public pages.
Say sample eval, not a universal industry benchmark.
Apache-2.0 CLI. Do not claim the hosted Team plane is open source.

modules.name: Nicos Catalog
modules.purpose: A portable Go software-catalog engine. A host supplies folder layout and data plugins. The engine validates records, indexes them, searches with BM25, builds a relationship graph, and fails a drift check when the catalog no longer matches the source files.
architecture: A small Provider interface injects records from YAML, JSON, Markdown, or static fixtures.
The engine validates typed entities, rejects duplicate IDs, and builds a relationship graph.
Derived state is byte-deterministic.
Drift fails closed when the index no longer matches source.
ProjectPublic emits a closed export that cannot encode private host fields.
decisions: Provider and layout injection so the core stays portable.
Closed public projection instead of filtering a private index after the fact.
Fail-closed drift as an operational check, not a dashboard suggestion.
Host policy, valuation, and personal telemetry stay out of the public core.
talking_points: Public Apache-2.0 engine, not the factory host.
Local production work indexes a 3,400+ entity corpus. That is a local-verified claim, not a SaaS customer count.
Demo entities are synthetic fixtures. The engine boundary is real.
Do not discuss host-only money models or private telemetry in a public interview.

practices.prompt: Explain the portable-core versus host-policy split and why drift fails closed.
Name the public install and demo command for Nicos Catalog.

modules.name: Openbook
modules.purpose: A TypeScript, React, and Convex realtime social application: identity, a friend graph, an audience-scoped feed, reactions, comments, notifications, and messages.
architecture: A React client talks to a Convex backend over reactive queries.
Visibility is enforced in one server function used by feed and profile queries.
Friendships and conversations are keyed by a sorted pair key.
Reaction and comment tallies move in the same mutation transaction as the child row.
Shared typed contracts cross the backend and the web app.
decisions: Server-side visibility so a hidden post never reaches a client.
Pair-keyed relationships make request, accept, and DM-open idempotent.
Transaction-exact counters instead of eventually consistent likes.
Reactive queries instead of sockets or polling.
talking_points: Full-stack pin beside docs-puller's AI-infrastructure story.
Audience boundaries live on the server, not only in the browser.
MIT public repository with a local self-hosted Convex path.
Do not invent engagement percentages or user counts.

practices.prompt: Explain how Openbook keeps friends-only posts off unauthorized clients.
Name the local self-host command path from the public README.

modules.name: agent-ops
modules.purpose: Local records of what an AI agent did on a machine. Seven receipt-backed questions: what it did, saw, may call, said, proved, how good the review is, and what is running now.
architecture: trace parses Claude Code and Codex session JSONL into a SQLite FTS5 index.
context emits budgeted hydration plus a receipt of included, omitted, and truncated chunks.
mcp evaluates server and tool pairs against a YAML policy and appends a JSONL audit line.
claims fail closed when a quantity is not on the allowlist.
evidence packs bind required paths to digest-backed manifests.
bench scores a reviewer against gold labels.
fleet merges slot files into one board.
decisions: Every answer is a local file, not a model claim about itself.
Missing evidence is a failure.
A policy deny exits non-zero so a shell guard can compose it.
Pure Go SQLite, no cgo.
talking_points: Proof is a receipt you can open later.
Do not let the model grade its own work.
This CLI is not the factory control-plane telemetry stack.
Fail-closed number checks stop unmeasured speed-up claims.

practices.prompt: Explain why agent-ops stores receipts instead of asking the model to score itself.
Name the public install and a first trace-discovery command.

modules.name: keepawake
modules.purpose: A small macOS-only power-state helper for deliberate closed-lid work. It combines pmset disablesleep with a managed caffeinate process so a Mac can keep running while the lid is closed.
architecture: on records the prior SleepDisabled setting before it changes the system.
A persistent caffeinate process is tracked with start identity, not only a PID.
Commands serialize on a lock. Failed transitions try to roll back.
status is read-only and reports ON, OFF, or PARTIAL.
off restores the recorded prior setting instead of assuming sleep was enabled.
decisions: Restore the prior power setting. Do not guess.
Refuse to signal a reused or unrelated process.
Old records without prior state fail safe and may stay PARTIAL.
off is part of the product because a closed lid has worse airflow.
talking_points: Native and systems breadth. It is not the hiring lead pin.
macOS only. Do not claim Linux or Windows support.
Always run keepawake off when finished.
Do not invent battery-hour or thermal outcome numbers.

practices.prompt: Explain the keepawake safety model: prior state, PID identity, and why off matters.
Name the read-only command that reports ON, OFF, or PARTIAL.

modules.name: JobKit
modules.purpose: A local-first Go job-search toolkit in one binary: trusted YAML profile, eligibility, saved searches, inbox, JD parse, fit scoring, tailored materials, an append-only tracker, and an evidence-linked interview coach.
architecture: Human-authored state is strict YAML. Machine contracts are versioned JSON. History is append-only JSONL.
Deterministic scoring is authoritative. Optional model feedback is advisory.
Coach import accepts public-scope evidence only and rejects private paths.
Study curriculum for the six job-search pins is embedded and separate from JD-tied decks.
Synthetic public fixtures stay separate from operator state.
decisions: Go and the standard library first. One binary.
Do not build another broad personal job-search CLI.
The claims gate fails closed on an untraceable number.
The localhost UI calls the same score and progress functions as the CLI.
talking_points: Public MIT CLI. Never publish operator state.
Coach study is the ordered pin rehearsal. Coach deck remains JD-tied interview practice.
Do not invent application outcome percentages.
This is not resume-suite and not a host-only money model.

practices.prompt: Explain how JobKit keeps interview claims honest and why study lives on the coach surface.
Name the JobKit command that lists the pin modules and the next incomplete practice.
